requirements.quote:
A server which is authenticating with a certificate MAY optionally
request a certificate from the client.  This message, if sent, MUST
follow EncryptedExtensions.
requirements.condition: a server sends CertificateRequest while authenticating with a certificate
requirements.forbidden_behavior: send CertificateRequest before or in place of EncryptedExtensions
requirements.why_checkable: The emitted handshake-message order can be inspected and tested.

requirements.condition: encoding or parsing a CertificateRequest message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reverse, omit, or add fields in the CertificateRequest structure
requirements.why_checkable: The wire parser and serializer expose the declared field order.

requirements.required_behavior: accept and encode a vector length from 0 through 255 octets
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encode or accept a certificate_request_context longer than 255 octets
requirements.why_checkable: Boundary tests can exercise the vector's explicit length range.

requirements.condition: encoding or parsing the CertificateRequest extensions vector
requirements.required_behavior: use an encoded vector length from 2 through 65535 octets
requirements.forbidden_behavior: encode or accept an extensions vector outside 2 through 65535 octets
requirements.why_checkable: The vector length has explicit lower and upper wire bounds.

requirements.quote:
certificate_request_context:  An opaque string which identifies the
certificate request and which will be echoed in the client's
Certificate message.
requirements.condition: a client sends Certificate in response to CertificateRequest
requirements.required_behavior: echo the CertificateRequest certificate_request_context in the client Certificate message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: use a different certificate_request_context in the response
requirements.why_checkable: A handshake trace can compare the request and response context bytes.

requirements.quote:
The certificate_request_context MUST be
unique within the scope of this connection (thus preventing replay
of client CertificateVerify messages).
requirements.condition: a server creates a CertificateRequest context
requirements.required_behavior: use a certificate_request_context not previously used on the connection
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reuse a certificate_request_context within the same connection
requirements.why_checkable: Generated contexts can be tracked per connection and checked for reuse.

requirements.quote:
This field SHALL be zero
length unless used for the post-handshake authentication exchanges
described in Section 4.6.2.
requirements.condition: CertificateRequest is not part of a post-handshake authentication exchange
requirements.why_checkable: The exchange phase and encoded vector length are directly observable.

requirements.quote:
When requesting post-handshake
authentication, the server SHOULD make the context unpredictable
to the client (e.g., by randomly generating it) in order to
prevent an attacker who has temporary access to the client's
private key from pre-computing valid CertificateVerify messages.
requirements.required_behavior: generate a certificate_request_context that is unpredictable to the client
requirements.forbidden_behavior: derive the context from a client-predictable sequence
requirements.why_checkable: The context-generation path can be inspected for cryptographic randomness or equivalent unpredictability.

requirements.quote:
The "signature_algorithms" extension
MUST be specified, and other extensions may optionally be included
if defined for this message.
requirements.why_checkable: The extension list can be inspected for required presence.

requirements.quote:
The "signature_algorithms" extension
MUST be specified, and other extensions may optionally be included
if defined for this message.
requirements.condition: a server includes an extension other than signature_algorithms in CertificateRequest
requirements.required_behavior: include only extensions defined for CertificateRequest
requirements.forbidden_behavior: include an extension not defined for CertificateRequest
requirements.why_checkable: The sender's extension allowlist can be compared with extensions defined for this message.

requirements.condition: a client parses an unrecognized CertificateRequest extension
requirements.forbidden_behavior: reject or alter handshake processing solely because the extension is unrecognized
requirements.why_checkable: A CertificateRequest with an unknown extension can be injected into a client handshake.

requirements.quote:
Servers which are authenticating with a PSK MUST NOT send the
CertificateRequest message in the main handshake, though they MAY
send it in post-handshake authentication (see Section 4.6.2) provided
that the client has sent the "post_handshake_auth" extension (see
Section 4.2.6).
requirements.condition: a server authenticates with a PSK during the main handshake
requirements.forbidden_behavior: send CertificateRequest in the main handshake
requirements.why_checkable: A PSK handshake trace can assert absence of the forbidden message.

requirements.quote:
Servers which are authenticating with a PSK MUST NOT send the
CertificateRequest message in the main handshake, though they MAY
send it in post-handshake authentication (see Section 4.6.2) provided
that the client has sent the "post_handshake_auth" extension (see
Section 4.2.6).
requirements.condition: a PSK-authenticating server sends a post-handshake CertificateRequest
requirements.required_behavior: send it only when the client previously sent the post_handshake_auth extension
requirements.forbidden_behavior: request post-handshake authentication without the client's post_handshake_auth offer
requirements.why_checkable: The post-handshake request can be correlated with the earlier ClientHello extension set.
